description: Test your knowledge of Lungs & Trachea anatomy and clinical correlations.

cards.text: What is the length and vertebral extent of the trachea?
cards.answer: The trachea is 10–11 cm long, extending from C6 (lower border of cricoid cartilage) to T4/T5 (carina). It is composed of 16–20 C-shaped hyaline cartilage rings.

tip.tip: C6 to T4/T5 — Remember: **C**ricoid (C6) to **T**horacic (T4/T5) vertebrae

cards.text: Why do foreign bodies preferentially lodge in the right main bronchus?
cards.answer: The right main bronchus is wider (2.5 cm), shorter (2.5 cm), and more vertical (25°) compared to the left. This straighter path makes aspiration into the right side more likely.

tip.tip: Right is **Wider, Shorter, Steeper** — the three W's of danger for aspiration

cards.text: At what anatomical level is a tracheostomy performed, and why?
cards.answer: Tracheostomy is performed between tracheal rings 2–4 (below the cricoid cartilage) to avoid the thyroid isthmus. Emergency cricothyrotomy is performed between rings 1–2.

tip.tip: Rings **2–4** avoid the thyroid; rings **1–2** for emergency (below cricoid)

cards.text: What is the role of the trachealis muscle, and what is its embryological origin?
cards.answer: The trachealis muscle is smooth muscle that bridges the posterior gap of the C-shaped cartilage rings. It allows the trachea to deform posteriorly, permitting the oesophagus to bulge anteriorly during swallowing.

tip.tip: Trachealis = **flexibility for swallowing** — smooth muscle allows deformation

cards.text: How many lobes and bronchopulmonary segments does each lung have?
cards.answer: Right lung: 3 lobes (upper, middle, lower) with **10 segments**. Left lung: 2 lobes (upper, lower) with **8–10 segments** (lingula functions as the middle lobe equivalent).

tip.tip: Right = **3-10**, Left = **2-8/10**; Lingula = Left's middle lobe substitute

cards.text: Why does tuberculosis preferentially affect the apical segments of the upper lobe?
cards.answer: The apical and posterior segments (S1, S2) of the upper lobe have the highest O₂ tension because ventilation exceeds perfusion at the apex (highest V/Q ratio). Mycobacterium tuberculosis is an obligate aerobe and thrives in high-oxygen environments.

tip.tip: **Apex = Highest O₂** → TB loves it. Remember: **V/Q highest at apex**

cards.text: What are the key anatomical relations of the left main bronchus in the thorax?
cards.answer: Anterior: arch of aorta; Posterior: oesophagus (slightly right of midline); Lateral: arch of aorta (left). Importantly, the left recurrent laryngeal nerve runs in the tracheo-oesophageal groove, making it vulnerable during thoracic surgery.

tip.tip: Left main bronchus = **Aorta in front, RLN in groove behind** — surgical landmark

cards.text: What structures pass through the hilum of the lung, and what is the typical order of structures at the right hilum (anterior to posterior)?
cards.answer: The hilum transmits: main bronchus, pulmonary artery, pulmonary veins (2 pairs), bronchial vessels, lymphatics, and autonomic nerves. At the right hilum (anterior to posterior): pulmonary veins, pulmonary artery, then main bronchus.

tip.tip: Remember **VAB** (anterior to posterior): **V**eins, **A**rtery, **B**ronchus — like an exam answer!
